caveats: Both rules assume the tests are independent and test the same one-sided hypothesis. Fisher is driven by the smallest p-values; Stouffer weighs every test, and with weights (for example the square root of each study's sample size) lets larger studies count more.

p_value is the upper tail of the statistic, so it tests one direction. Two-sided p-values given without their effects are combined as if one-sided, and opposite effects then reinforce each other instead of cancelling: give each test's effect for that.
Neither rule estimates an effect size; pool the estimates with stats meta for that. p_value is not adjusted across features; send the p_value column to stats adjust.

Each p-value was read as two-sided and converted with the sign of its effect (mzLib's PValueCombination.OneSided): p/2 for a positive effect, 1 - p/2 for a negative one. p_value therefore tests effect > 0, and a p_value near 1 means a consistently negative effect. A test whose effect is 0, blank or NA has no direction and is omitted.
For a negative effect whose two-sided p-value is below about 2e-16, 1 - p/2 rounds to 1, so that test's z is minus infinity and decides the feature (p_value 1).
